consensus_summary: Mainstream Christian reading treats foreskin/uncircumcision primarily as the unregenerate sinful flesh or a hardened, spiritually insensitive heart (and by extension ears/lips), marking impurity, stubborn resistance to God, and covenant alienation; physical removal typifies inward cleansing and heart-circumcision by the Spirit. Ethnic-outsider, ritual-impurity, impediment, shame, and typological senses are common complementary uses.
book_summary: Foreskin is obstructing flesh that covers a covenant member and blocks its proper work; heart, ear, lips, and fruit are called uncircumcised when flesh prevents humility, hearing, speech, or fruitfulness.
consensus_core_identification: Sinful/unregenerate flesh or hardened spiritual resistance (heart/ears etc.) whose removal signifies cleansing and covenant consecration.
book_core_identification: Obstructing flesh covering a covenant member and preventing its proper covenantal work (humility, hearing, speech, fruitfulness).
boundary_disagreement: Book centers a single functional-obstruction model on covenant faculties (heart, ear, lips, fruit) and frames the covered subject as a covenant member; it does not take ethnic-outsider status, general covenant exclusion, or bare ‘sinful nature’ as the primary symbolic identity, though those remain nearby in the cited texts.
material_contradiction: None. The book does not deny hardness, impurity, or the need to put off flesh; it re-specifies the same covering as obstruction of proper work.
rationale: Minimum cores share the same referent class: flesh that must be cut away so heart/ear/lips (and related faculties) function rightly before God. Consensus states this mainly as unregenerate nature, stubbornness, and alienation; the book preserves that category but tightens it to ‘obstructing cover on a covenant member preventing proper work,’ unifies fruit under the same pattern, and shifts emphasis away from outsider-label and pure moral-state formulations. That is refinement of boundary and precision, not replacement of the core.
strongest_objection: Consensus often treats ‘the uncircumcision’ as a primary ethnic/covenantal outsider label and the foreskin as the sinful nature itself; the book’s ‘covenant member + functional obstruction’ framing could be charged with sidelining those dominant senses.
